_note: Read-the-monitor scenarios. For study only, not clinical guidance. Each scenario maps to one library category (must match a name in assets/catalog.js). 'answer' is the zero-based index of the correct option.

scenarios.title: Tachycardia at rest
options: Rate problem with normal oxygenation: work up the cause, check the ECG rhythm
Hypoxic emergency: high-flow oxygen first, the rate is secondary
scenarios.why: Heart rate 128 with normal saturation, temperature and pressure is a rate problem to work up, not a hypoxic one. Confirm the rhythm on the ECG, then look for the usual drivers.

scenarios.title: Hypoxaemia with tachypnoea
options: Normal for a fit young adult
Respiratory problem with falling oxygen: give oxygen and find the cause
scenarios.why: Saturation 86 with a respiratory rate of 28 is a gas-exchange problem. Oxygen and a cause hunt come before anything else on this monitor.

scenarios.title: Low pressure with tachycardia
options: Low pressure with compensatory tachycardia: treat as possible shock until proven otherwise
Normal resting pressure, the reading is artefact
scenarios.why: A falling pressure with a rising heart rate is the compensated pattern. The pressure drops late, so the early sign is the rate. Treat the pattern as shock until the cause is clear.

scenarios.title: Fever with a rising rate
options: Fever with tachycardia: look for a source and document the trend
scenarios.why: A temperature of 38.6 with a heart rate of 112 is a febrile response. The task is the source and the trend, not the number on its own.

scenarios.title: Bradycardia with a pressure drop
options: Hypoxic emergency: high-flow oxygen first, the pulse is secondary
Symptomatic bradycardia: check perfusion and the ECG, treat if unstable
scenarios.why: A rate of 38 with a falling pressure needs perfusion and rhythm checked now. Treatment follows instability, so the ECG decides what happens next.

scenarios.title: Deep, rapid, laboured breathing
options: Deep, rapid, laboured breathing: compensation for a metabolic acidosis
scenarios.why: Deep, rapid breathing is the respiratory compensation for a metabolic acidosis. It is the pattern to recognise, and the cause is the target.

scenarios.title: Cold, slow and drifting
options: Hypothermia with bradycardia: rewarm and recheck the rhythm
scenarios.why: A core temperature of 34.8 with a slow rate and slow breathing points to hypothermia. Rewarming and a repeat rhythm check come first.

scenarios.title: Fever, rate, breathing and pressure together
options: Anxiety with a normal temperature: reassure
Possible sepsis: fever, tachycardia, tachypnoea and low pressure together, escalate
scenarios.why: Four abnormal signs at once is the early-warning pattern for sepsis. The framework says escalate now and do not wait for the numbers to get worse.

scenarios.title: Slow, shallow breathing with falling saturation
options: Reduced respiratory drive: oxygen, airway support and find the cause
scenarios.why: A respiratory rate of 8 with saturation falling to 91 is reduced drive, the sign of opioid or sedative effect. Oxygen and airway support come first, then the cause.

scenarios.title: Fast and irregularly irregular
options: Sinus arrhythmia: normal in young adults
Irregularly irregular rhythm at a fast rate: confirm on ECG and check for atrial fibrillation
Artefact from movement: ignore the trace
scenarios.why: An irregularly irregular rhythm at a fast rate on the trace is the pattern to confirm on a 12-lead ECG. The pulse trace shows the same beat-to-beat variation.
